correctness.rationale: The source gain reduces exactly to \(r_S=(\mu^2+v)/(\mu^2+v/S)\) because both expectation terms share the state factor. The batch-average curvature has moments \(\mu\) and \(\mu^2+v/S\), so conditioning gives the stated scalar second-moment multiplier. Its sign relative to one factors into a positive scale term times \(\alpha^2(\mu^2+v)-2\alpha\mu\), proving the if-and-only-if frontier, equality boundary, supercritical growth, and scale-independent optimizer.

value.rationale: AdaScale was designed specifically to adapt learning rates to variance reduction from larger parallel batches while avoiding the failures of fixed linear scaling. The exact random-curvature law shows that its defining gain accomplishes a sharp and interpretable task: it preserves the entire single-batch mean-square stability interval at every scale, while the optimally tuned expected-objective contraction improves strictly with scale. The linear-scaling comparator proves that this invariance is not automatic under batch averaging.
